evals.prompt: /code-quality — do a full quality audit of this repo. Python service, about 90 source files under src/ and 40 test modules under tests/, pytest suite takes ~25s. Audit only for now, don't change anything.
evals.expected_output: Runs Phase 0 ONCE (scope, language set, baseline suite, report dirs) and builds the shared index (file list + import graph + symbol index) before any lens runs. Fans out seven analyzers in parallel with that index, then seven reviewers, then one consolidator. Emits a single merged CODE-QUALITY-REPORT, reaps the seven per-lens drafts, and stops at the decision gate honouring 'audit only'.
assertions: Runs the shared Phase 0 exactly once itself (scope + detected language set + baseline test run + report dirs) rather than letting each lens re-scan
Builds all three shared-index artifacts in Phase 0 — scoped file list, import graph, and symbol index — and hands them to every analyzer
Scopes the test tree into the inventory too (does not exclude tests/ the way a production-only pass would)
Creates docs/reports/code-quality/ plus a docs/reports/<lens>/ dir for each of the seven lenses
Dispatches seven analyzer subagents in parallel, one per lens, each pointed at skills/<lens>/agents/analyzer.md — including acceptance-quality, which auto-skips if no acceptance suite is found
Cuts the worktree set itself at the reviewed ref (lens_worktrees.py) and dispatches WITHOUT the harness's isolation: flag, rather than letting seven writing agents share one tree
Gives code paths repo-relative and the draft path as an injected artifact root, and requires each analyzer to assert its scoped files resolve under its own working directory before reading
Passes ddd in analyze mode only (never design or build) and clean-code in deep gear (not the inline quick gear)
Does not dispatch analyzers with a read-only agent type (Explore) — each must be able to write its own draft-findings.md
Dispatches seven reviewers, and tells the gof reviewer to skip its HTML preview and write only Markdown
Dispatches one consolidator that merges into a single docs/reports/code-quality/CODE-QUALITY-REPORT-<date>.md
Deletes each lens's draft-findings.md only after the consolidated report exists and parses
Treats 'audit only' as the human review and stops at the report without applying anything
Adds no findings of its own — every finding traces to a lens reviewer
Fills the report's ## Measurements section from the Phase 0 readout, and omits any sensor that could not run rather than printing a number for it
Leaves --mutation off unless asked — whole-repo mutation is a cost the operator chooses, never a silent Phase 0 default

REVIEWER DISCRIMINATION — the reviewer visibly overturns the analyzer on at least one finding (prunes it with a stated reason, re-tiers it, or merges a double-filed smell), and says so in the report. A reviewer that kept every draft finding unchanged scores the same as one that verified nothing, which defeats the generator/critic split

evals.prompt: /code-quality — full audit, and I pre-approve applying everything Critical and Major, including grouped changes. Don't stop to ask me. Same Python repo, pytest.
evals.expected_output: Same fan-out and consolidation, then applies through the shared TDD engine on one code-quality/<slug> branch: apply order taken from the report's Findings index, each finding dispatched through its ORIGINATING lens's implementer (a test-quality rec goes to test-quality's implementer with its mutation + coverage gates), implementer model tiered by Risk, checkpoint commits between jobs, and an ## Outcome section persisted into the report.
assertions: Treats the pre-authorization as the Phase 3 human review and does not re-ask for approval of Critical/Major
Still resolves any explicit ## Conflicts fork with the human — a blanket tier approval does not satisfy a fork
Applies in the order the report's Findings index computed, rather than re-deriving a Critical-then-Major order
Dispatches each approved finding through its originating lens's agents/implementer.md, falling back to the shared implementer only where the lens ships none
Routes any test-quality finding through skills/test-quality/agents/implementer.md so its mutation and coverage-non-regression gates stay wired
Tiers the implementer model by Risk (Low/Med/High) and never drops below sonnet where characterization pins are needed
Checkpoint-commits each verified job on a single code-quality/<slug> working branch
Runs the full suite at Phase 5 and writes an ## Outcome section into the consolidated report (applied / deferred / failed, suite before -> after)
Does not auto-commit or auto-publish — offers /ship instead

Reads the apply order off the Findings index rather than re-deriving it — where a Major must land before a Critical because the Critical's fix depends on it, the index order and a plain Critical→Major sort disagree, and only reading the index gets it right

evals.prompt: /code-quality on this repo. Heads up: it's a Python + TypeScript monorepo, there's no graphify-out/graph.json, and I know the ddd analyzer has been crashing on our tree lately. (Assume the ddd analyzer writes its draft-findings.md successfully and then crashes before returning — so there IS a draft to preserve.)
evals.expected_output: Handles both degradations without treating either as a blocker: no structural graph means starting the shared-index ladder one rung down (ast-grep -> ctags -> agent-read) and recording a coverage note; a lens that dies is a loudly-recorded coverage gap in the consolidated report, its draft kept as the sole evidence, and its artifact is never written on its behalf.
assertions: Treats an absent graphify-out/graph.json as ordinary — works the fallback ladder (ast-grep, then ctags, then agent-read) rather than blocking or demanding a graph
Records the missing structural graph as a Coverage note, and passes a structural-graph verdict of None to every analyzer
Loads each lens's references/<language>.md for BOTH detected languages (python and typescript), degrading gracefully where a lens has none
Records a dead or failed lens as an explicit Coverage gap in the consolidated report rather than silently omitting it
Does NOT write the failed lens's draft-findings.md or report on its behalf — re-dispatches or records the gap
Keeps the failed lens's draft-findings.md rather than reaping it, since no dated report exists for that lens
Proceeds with the remaining lenses instead of aborting the whole audit

evals.prompt: Two requests to route against the installed skill set: (1) "our test suite is a total mess, tests everywhere, half of them probably dead — can you clean it up?" and (2) "review the diff on my feature branch before I open the PR." For each, say which skill should handle it and why.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes both as NOT the umbrella. (1) is a scoped one-concern request -> /test-quality even though the user never named the lens. (2) is a change-set correctness review -> /code-review, not a whole-codebase architecture-and-craft audit. Explains the carve rather than running seven lenses.
assertions: Routes request (1) to /test-quality, explicitly because it is scoped to one concern even though the lens is never named
Routes request (2) to /code-review, explicitly because a diff/PR correctness pass is not what /code-quality does
Does not launch the seven-lens fan-out for either request
States the carve: the umbrella is for a whole-codebase audit spanning multiple concerns, not a scoped one-concern pass or a change-set bug review

evals.prompt: /code-quality over all commits ahead of origin/main, and give each agent its own worktree. (The harness cuts those worktrees at the merge-base, so the branch's code is not in them.)
evals.expected_output: Every lens stops on the missing subject and reports a named coverage gap, rather than re-resolving the scoped files against the orchestrator's checkout by absolute path and reporting a clean isolated run over code it never had.
assertions: Each analyzer asserts the scoped files resolve under its own working directory before reading, and stops when they do not
No lens re-resolves its scoped files against the orchestrator's checkout by absolute path to keep working
The absent code is reported as a named coverage gap per lens, never as a completed audit
test-quality is not treated as the only affected lens — its mutation gate merely fails first because it must execute the code
Drafts are written to the injected artifact root, which is outside the worktree and so survives the worktree being cleaned up
Does not present the consolidated report as a full seven-lens audit when lenses could not read their subject
